A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable main text, equations, experiments, figures, tables, and Appendices A-N. Content can be matched across the added pages and renumbered figures.

before.justification: Section 6 and the appendices report original Gaussian simulations, CIFAR-10, MUSIC and SC09 evaluations, and optimization timings.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds AFHQv2 evaluations and experiments on accelerating schedule optimization.

M1.justification: Appendix N introduces iterative initialization using interpolated solutions from smaller diffusion-step counts. It also evaluates PCA reduction, previously suggested as a possible strategy. The core spectral formulation, losses, and SLSQP optimizer remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v3 retains the synthetic Gaussian, CIFAR-10, MUSIC and SC09 coverage and adds AFHQv2 image generation in Appendix J. Its 64 x 64 images extend the image-data coverage beyond the existing CIFAR-10 experiments.

E2.justification: The linear, EDM, cosine, sigmoid, and simplified AYS comparisons are retained. The new AFHQv2 experiment uses the same heuristic methods; its EDM rho=5 configuration is an experimental-setting difference.

E3.justification: The added AFHQv2 evaluation uses 64 x 64 images, EDM rho=5, and step counts {10,20,30,40,50,70,90,112}. Appendix N adds random-versus-iterative initialization comparisons and optimization with 3,072 PCA components. Existing experimental settings are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix N extends the runtime analysis to larger covariance matrices and tests whether iterative initialization and PCA reduce optimization cost. The existing constraint, initialization, spectral-dynamics, mean-bias, and DDPM-versus-DDIM analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report three independent CIFAR-10 runs and mean plus or minus 95% confidence intervals using standard errors and the t-distribution in Tables 1-2. The added experiments introduce no new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: v3 adds AFHQv2 Wasserstein-2/FID curves and acceleration timings while retaining existing results. Table 4 reports 50-step timings of 93.09 seconds for random initialization, 43.52 cumulatively for iterative initialization, and 12.71 for PCA. The new 250-step random-initialization value is inconsistent: 7417.46 in Table 3 versus 74117.47 in Table 4.

T1.justification: The Gaussian assumptions, transfer-function theorems, Wasserstein-2/KL derivations, VP/VE formulations, and appendix proofs are unchanged. Gaussian mixtures are mentioned only as future work, without a new formal extension.

C1.justification: The abstract and four stated contributions remain unchanged. Section 7 adds explicit claims of FID advantages across multiple datasets and optimization reduced to a few tens of seconds; v2 presented PCA acceleration only as a possible remedy.

C2.justification: Section 7 newly identifies Gaussian-mixture extensions as a way to better represent real distributions. The runtime discussion shifts from suggesting mitigation to claiming demonstrated acceleration, supported by the expanded Appendix N.

D1.justification: v3 documents AFHQv2's 12,288-dimensional covariance, its 2,000-iteration or 1e-6 tolerance stopping criteria, iterative interpolation, and retention of 3,072 PCA components. Existing training details, CIFAR-10 schedule vectors, and resource links are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Choi et al.'s StarGAN v2 reference for AFHQv2. The related-work discussion and positioning against earlier scheduling and Gaussian-analysis research remain unchanged apart from citation renumbering.

P1.justification: Rewriting is concentrated in Section 7 and Appendix N, with an added AFHQv2 paragraph and an updated introductory dataset list. The overall narrative, section order, and appendix organization remain stable.

P2.justification: v3 adds the two-panel Figure 21, an AFHQv2 column in Table 3, and Table 4. Later figures are renumbered and some material moves across pages. All 79 pre-existing plot images are retained unchanged.

improvement.justification: The AFHQv2 evaluation broadens empirical support, and the acceleration experiments provide practical evidence beyond v2's untested PCA suggestion. The core analysis remains intact. Benefits are tempered by the conflicting 250-step timings in Tables 3-4 and the absence of a quantified sample-quality comparison for PCA, but the focused additions provide a modest net improvement.
